meetings.summary: The select board discussed two special town meeting articles at length: one restoring cut middle/high school sports funding (Article 3, championed by a parent petitioner) and one using additional state aid to supplement the FY27 school budget (Article One), voting to recommend a lower net figure for Article One and creating a special revenue fund seeded from Winter Recovery Assistance Program money to help fund Article 3. The board also approved a toll-booth fundraiser permit, heard from a new principal assessor, sent a letter supporting the Question 1 legislative audit, received a town manager's report flagging unexpended FY26 school funds and a planned financial review, and approved prior minutes before adjourning.

budget_items.topic: Comment on a school committee remark about a small dollar figure
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member said he was troubled by a school committee comment suggesting the town shouldn't squabble over a small sum, arguing that amount is close to a full year's tax bill for modest homes. He urged the board to treat every dollar residents send in as significant.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 - original ask to restore cut sports
budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner's original citizen petition sought funding to restore all cut middle and high school sports, including transportation, based on figures obtained from the school department.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 - high school transportation removed from article
budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner removed high school athletic transportation from his article after the district separately arranged and funded that transportation.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 - revised total pending school committee credit
budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner said the school committee was expected to vote the next night to give a credit toward Article 3, which would reduce the net amount requested in the article.

budget_items.topic: Athletic transportation budget line
budget_items.what_was_said: A finance committee slide showed the original athletic transportation line that had been cut from the FY27 budget; the high school portion was later restored using a mix of the athletic revolving fund and additional state aid freed up by a reading grant.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 - petitioner's transportation estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner's own estimate for combined high school and middle school athletic transportation was higher than the figure the district later produced for the high school portion alone.

budget_items.topic: Athletic participation fees
budget_items.what_was_said: Board members and the petitioner discussed current and expected athletic fees, noting the middle school fee for winter and spring was not yet published because there is no middle school season this fall.

budget_items.topic: Middle school track program revenue
budget_items.what_was_said: The petitioner said one middle school sport generated a net positive contribution to the athletic program at last year's fee, while middle school sports as a group were not net positive once officials, trainers and field costs are allocated.

budget_items.topic: Article One - state aid to supplement FY27 school budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The school department's article requests use of additional state aid to supplement the FY27 operating budget, under a spending plan the school committee has already voted and the finance committee recommended.

budget_items.topic: Article One - dispute over net vs. gross state aid
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member argued the requested figure improperly folds in cherry sheet offsets tied to school choice and charter tuition assessments, which are not school operating line increases, and that the true net education aid available is lower.

budget_items.topic: Article One - board's recommended amount
budget_items.what_was_said: A motion was made to recommend town meeting approve Article One at the lower net figure rather than the school department's full requested amount.

budget_items.topic: FY26 preliminary year-end update
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported a preliminary projection of unexpended FY26 school department appropriations, part of a larger unexpended total across the whole town budget, cautioning the numbers will still move during closeout.

budget_items.topic: FY26 funds moved from operating budget to a grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said a specific amount originally budgeted in the operating budget has already been identified as having been moved out to a grant.

budget_items.topic: Municipal electricity aggregation rate
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported new 24-month aggregation supply pricing through First Point Power, lower than the utility's default rate but higher than the town's prior aggregation rate, citing global market volatility.

budget_items.topic: Personnel committee - classification and compensation study
budget_items.what_was_said: The personnel committee is considering warrant articles for the November special town meeting, including a request to fund a comprehensive classification and compensation study.

budget_items.topic: FY26 snow and ice deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager presented the estimated FY26 snow and ice deficit, noting the number still needs to be finalized once DPW overtime wages under a newly settled labor contract are reconciled retroactively.

budget_items.topic: Free cash already applied to the snow/ice deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting in May already appropriated free cash toward the snow and ice deficit, leaving a remaining balance before the state's winter recovery money is applied.

budget_items.topic: RAP (Winter Recovery Assistance Program) funds received
budget_items.what_was_said: The town received a specific amount of state RAP money; DLS strongly recommended using it to fully cure the remaining FY26 snow and ice deficit.

budget_items.topic: RAP balance remaining after curing the deficit
budget_items.what_was_said: After applying RAP money to the snow and ice deficit, a remaining balance would be available for the board to split between FY26 free cash and a new special revenue fund.

budget_items.topic: Proposed RAP split to fund Article 3
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager proposed sending part of the remaining RAP balance to a new special revenue fund to serve as the funding source for Article 3, with the remainder going to free cash.

budget_items.topic: Amount to seed the special revenue fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The board settled on an amount to seed the new special revenue fund intended to fund Article 3, rounding to account for the school committee's expected credit.

budget_items.topic: Water department quarterly billing commitment
budget_items.what_was_said: The board signed a notice of water commitment for the first quarterly billing of fiscal year 2027.

budget_items.topic: Public comment - school funding shortfall
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident argued the schools are operating with significantly less funding than the level-service budget required, and urged that the net increase in state aid go entirely to the school department given the size of that gap.

decisions.decision: The school committee agreed it would spend Article 3 funds as described in the article if it passes, since legally the money becomes an unrestricted supplement to the school budget that the school committee controls.

The town will pursue an independent financial reconciliation and budget review of FY26 school finances, with a consulting-firm call scheduled for Friday and funding to be sought first through the finance committee's reserve fund and, if that fails, at the November special town meeting.
The board agreed to hold its next select board chat/office-hours session on Wednesday, September 30th, from 6 to 7pm, likely at the library since the usual coffee shop closes early.

The stormwater task force will hold a public information session in late October or early November, before the November special town meeting, and will bring its draft non-binding article back through the finance committee (around October 8th) and the select board (around October 20th).
Confirmed that the town now officially owns the property being discussed for the TC Patio senior housing proposal.

meetings.summary: This was a Finance Committee meeting doubling as a public hearing on three special town meeting articles: article 1 to appropriate new state aid to the school department's revised spending plan (including a second-grade teacher, reading specialist, assistant principal, and restored athletic transportation), article 2 (a substantively similar citizen petition article that the petitioner asked to have passed over in favor of article 1), and article 3 (a citizen petition to fund middle and high school sports and transportation, with its final funding mechanism still unresolved). The committee voted to recommend approval of article 1, to defer article 2 and article 3 to town meeting pending firmer numbers, and separately approved prior minutes and adjourned.

budget_items.topic: Ignite tutoring seats funding freed up by state grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said the original spending plan had set aside a Ignite tutoring seats amount that was freed up once the district received a state grant covering 36 seats instead of the full ask. That freed amount became the basis for three reallocation scenarios brought to school committee.

budget_items.topic: Athletics revolving account balance
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent gave the current revolving account status for athletics as of 8/13 and the amount expended from it so far, to set up why the plan proposes drawing from that account for transportation.

budget_items.topic: High school athletic transportation cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Originally budgeted athletic transportation cost was cut roughly in half after a zero-based budgeting exercise using actual quotes and last year's actuals; the superintendent attributed savings to the former and current athletic directors' work with the bus vendor.

budget_items.topic: Article 1 total spending plan / transportation line split
budget_items.what_was_said: On the spending-plan slide only part of the transportation savings is shown, with the remainder proposed to come out of the athletic revolving account; the slide totals the whole article 1 ask.

budget_items.topic: School choice credit ($5,541) folded into article 1 calculus
budget_items.what_was_said: A selectman flagged that a school-choice-credit figure included in the article 1 total is not actually subject to town-meeting appropriation because it goes directly to the school department. Officials discussed leaving article 1's total as written and instead using this amount to offset article 3.

budget_items.topic: Estimated cost of a district financial audit
budget_items.what_was_said: Asked whether there was a cost estimate for the proposed comprehensive audit, the superintendent said she had been benchmarking a figure but would not know for certain until quotes/proposals came back; a board member noted a request for proposals may not even be required for this type of consulting.

budget_items.topic: Out-of-district special education placement costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said three new out-of-district placements were identified last week, and gave an average per-placement cost including transportation as justification for prioritizing a behavior analyst position to try to prevent further placements.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 sports/transportation funding figure (school committee number)
budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee arrived at a figure representing middle school sports plus certain restored high school sports and their transportation, after excluding sports too late to arrange transportation for.

budget_items.topic: Article 3 net amount after school-choice offset
budget_items.what_was_said: There is a handshake agreement, still needing school committee ratification, to backfill the sports figure using the school-choice-credit amount discussed earlier, which would lower the amount actually needed from article 3.

budget_items.topic: Middle school sports/transportation cost breakdown
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member asked the petitioner to confirm that a specific figure covers middle school basketball and outdoor track plus their transportation; the petitioner said that was his understanding from the school department's numbers.

budget_items.topic: Article 1 warrant amount as moved
budget_items.what_was_said: The article was moved as written in the warrant at the total figure discussed all evening; the committee recommended approval of that figure.

budget_items.topic: Additional cherry sheet money beyond the article 1 figure
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member explained that more state-aid money is available on the cherry sheets than what was tallied into article 1's total, and using article 3 would effectively draw on and credit back some of that broader pool.

transfers.description: Proposed use of an available funding source such as the RAP special fund to reduce the amount required on article 3 by the school-choice-credit amount already on the school department's books
Select board would need to first establish a special purpose fund from RAP (revolving/athletic-type) funds before any transfer could be made to fund article 3
School committee handshake agreement, pending Wednesday ratification, to use the school-choice-credit amount to backfill/reduce the article 3 sports figure
Money drawn into article 1 from broader cherry-sheet state aid sources would effectively be credited back if article 3 passes

decisions.decision: Committee chairs (select board, school committee, town manager) reached a general agreement to leave the article 1 warrant figure as originally calculated and instead use the school-choice-credit amount to reduce what article 3 needs to raise.
The superintendent stated she will not return unspent article 1 funds to the town if freed up by new grants; she will publicly reallocate them within other district priorities.

The school committee affirmed the prior night that if article 3 passes, the funds will be spent on sports in keeping with the article's intent, even though the town cannot legally earmark school committee spending.
The finance committee decided to skip a separate pre-town-meeting sit-down and instead caucus informally in the room shortly before or during the special town meeting itself.
The town manager will proceed with scheduling informational (non-deliberative) sessions with Department of Revenue subject matter experts on RAP funds.

meetings.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee heard extended public comment on staff turnover, reading scores, and school funding, then reviewed three alternative spending scenarios for additional state aid to be requested at a special town meeting: an independent financial audit, a second-grade teacher plus literacy support, or an additional behavior analyst, each paired with restoring high school athletic transportation. The committee voted to bring the scenario adding a second-grade teacher and literacy professional development to finance committee, discussed two town-meeting warrant articles (one on financial transparency to be passed over, one a citizens' petition to fund middle school sports restoration), and voted to support the spirit of the sports-funding petition if town meeting appropriates outside money, without committing the schools' own fund balances.

budget_items.topic: Ignite tutoring grant/seats
budget_items.what_was_said: A parent asked whether the district would stay with the state grant's seat count or add more seats funded from elsewhere in the budget, since prior spending plans approved by the committee had proposed larger seat counts.

budget_items.topic: Athletic transportation line, FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: A commenter noted the FY27 budget line covered high school and middle school athletic transportation combined, and questioned how the restoration figure could be so much lower and why it wasn't found during FY27 budget building.

budget_items.topic: School fund balances (school choice revolving, circuit breaker, gift fund, after-school activities)
budget_items.what_was_said: A commenter listed several school-controlled fund balances as of a recent date and suggested drawing modest amounts from each to help fund middle school sports restoration.

budget_items.topic: State aid request vs. school choice/charter assessment increase and receiving tuition
budget_items.what_was_said: A commenter said the requested state-aid figure does not account for an increase in school choice/charter sending tuition owed to the state, and that it includes a receiving-tuition amount that goes to the district automatically without town meeting appropriation.

budget_items.topic: Level-services funding shortfall
budget_items.what_was_said: A commenter said the schools received far less than needed to maintain FY26-level services and urged the town to focus on that larger shortfall rather than smaller disputed amounts.

budget_items.topic: Ignite tutoring seat cost and funds freed
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said the district will keep the grant-funded seat count and not fund additional seats, which frees money from the original ask to redirect to other scenarios.

budget_items.topic: Scenario 1: independent financial audit + athletic transportation
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed an RFP for an independent financial audit of the schools plus restoring athletic transportation, funded partly from new town-meeting money and partly from the athletic revolving account.

budget_items.topic: Athletic revolving account balance and spending
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent gave the verified balance of the athletic revolving account as of a mid-August date and the amount spent so far this year, to show it could help cover transportation.

budget_items.topic: Athletic transportation cost estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said a vendor gave an approximate transportation cost which she rounded up to allow for incidentals.

budget_items.topic: Scenario 2: grade 2 class size reduction + literacy PD
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed using freed funds to add a second-grade teacher and extend literacy professional-development support to the middle and high school, plus the athletic transportation restoration.

budget_items.topic: Scenario 3: additional BCBA hire
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed hiring a second board-certified behavior analyst, priced higher than a teacher line due to certification level, alongside the athletic transportation restoration.

budget_items.topic: Out-of-district placement costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said out-of-district placements are rising and gave rough average costs per placement including transportation and bus monitors, to justify the BCBA scenario.

budget_items.what_was_said: The article as read proposes transferring a specific sum from certified free cash to the FY27 school operating budget to restore middle school sports and provide student-athlete transportation.

budget_items.topic: Middle school sports restoration cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member relayed that a lower figure would restore basketball and outdoor track for middle school (cross country and field hockey could not be scheduled), and a higher figure would add lacrosse and ski at the high school level.

budget_items.topic: Breakdown of middle school sports restoration figure
budget_items.what_was_said: A committee member itemized the components behind the middle-school restoration estimate: coaching stipends at the top CBA step, transportation, and officials/entry fees.

budget_items.topic: High school lacrosse and ski co-op costs
budget_items.what_was_said: The athletic director's figures for last year's ski co-op invoices and girls lacrosse transportation and coaching were cited as the basis for the additional high-school restoration amount.

meetings.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee reviewed FY26 year-end line item transfers, approved several donations (LEAF grants, Musicators, football boosters), heard a detailed presentation on additional FY27 state aid via the cherry sheet, and voted to amend its warrant article for the September 3 "extra special" town meeting from $350,000 to $418,056 in additional state education aid. Amend the FY27 school department warrant article amount from $350,000 to $418,056 (as heard, "4418,56") for the September 3 special town meeting

Accept the new custodians' union (AFSCME Council 93) contract/MOU changes

budget_items.topic: Cherry sheet education-line increases, FY27 governor's budget vs. final budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through the difference between the governor's initial FY27 local aid proposal and the final signed budget for chapter 70, charter tuition reimbursement, and smart growth school reimbursement. She noted charter tuition and smart growth are highly variable year to year while school choice receipts have generally been declining.

budget_items.topic: Total cherry sheet receipts increase
budget_items.what_was_said: The total increase across all cherry sheet receipt lines (education plus small increases in UGGA and aid for the visually impaired/elderly) was given as this figure.

budget_items.topic: State assessments/charges increase (school choice and charter sending tuition)
budget_items.what_was_said: School choice sending tuition decreased while charter school sending tuition increased, netting to this additional assessment amount, the only assessments that rose being education-related.

budget_items.topic: Net additional state aid available to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: Subtracting the extra assessments from the extra receipts yields the town's net additional state aid for FY27, framed as the basis for the school committee's funding request.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: maintenance of buildings to grounds contracted services
budget_items.what_was_said: Transfer to cover a grounds contracted-services overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: maintenance salaries to maintenance overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: Transfer to cover a maintenance overtime overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: custodian salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from middle and high school custodian lines to elementary and primary school custodian lines to cover overages.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: athletic security/detail
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from athletic transportation to special detail (police) at athletic events to cover an overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: regular transportation
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from heating charges to regular transportation; business manager said the transportation line had simply been budgeted too low the prior year, and it has since been revised for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school guidance salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from middle school guidance counselors to high school guidance counselor and secretary lines; attributed partly to costs from summer scheduling issues.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school substitutes
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from long-term substitutes to regular substitutes to cover an overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school principal/assistant principal salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from a middle school administrative secretary line; described as a line that had been budgeted too low, now corrected for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: special education paraprofessionals and hospital tutoring
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from a high school special education resource room teacher line (attributed to a staff leave of absence) to hospital tutoring and special ed paraprofessional lines across several schools.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: superintendent general supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from dues and meetings to general supplies, attributed to unused conference/meeting funds.

budget_items.topic: FY26 year-end budget spend rate
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager reported total expenses came in at about this percentage of budget, with salaries still being finalized and expected to land close to but under 100%.

budget_items.topic: Prior-year budget overage (context for the shortfall crisis)
budget_items.what_was_said: Referencing the overage that caused a earlier-year budget crisis, a member asked what share of the budget it represented; the business manager estimated it at around 2.5%, expecting this year's number to be smaller.

budget_items.topic: LEAF grants (Lunenburg Education Accelerator Foundation)
budget_items.what_was_said: LEAF's first year of fundraising produced six grants for classroom/program items (sound system, erector sets, STEM materials, magazine subscriptions), totaling this amount.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Musicators donations
budget_items.what_was_said: The Musicators donated $300 for color guard uniforms/gloves (citing a tripling of band/color guard membership) and $1,213 to fund the middle school jazz band stipend.

budget_items.topic: Football helmets donation, withdrawn
budget_items.what_was_said: Football boosters had offered to buy extra helmets, but because helmets are integral to safety the district will pay for them instead, so that donation was withdrawn.

budget_items.topic: Football/cheer away-game transportation donation
budget_items.what_was_said: With transportation cut from the athletic budget, the football boosters will fund two buses for away games (football and cheerleaders), split into three separate donations to preserve some booster treasury funds for the season.

budget_items.topic: FY27 technology/infrastructure earmark from Senator Cronin's office
budget_items.what_was_said: The district received notice of a state earmark for system infrastructure upgrades; the superintendent will work with technology and buildings/grounds staff on a spending plan.

budget_items.topic: ESSER/Title grant allocations
budget_items.what_was_said: Title II and Title IV allocations were relatively flat ($28,443 and $15,19 as heard); Title I came in far higher than the $96,000 the district had budgeted for, at $193,820, reason unknown to the superintendent.

budget_items.topic: Warrant article amount for additional state aid to schools
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman proposed increasing the previously-passed $350,000 warrant article to $418,000 (the legislature's increase to Lunenburg schools above the governor's budget) or as much as $475,000 (total town-wide increase); she noted the district also cut over $800,000 this year and that a further roughly $300,000 in one-time state money exists that she is not requesting.

budget_items.topic: Proposed use of the additional $68,000 (difference between $350,000 and $418,000)
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed using the incremental funds to restore a certified occupational therapy assistant (COTA) position, needed in part due to a new unfunded state mandate eliminating school "cool down rooms."

budget_items.topic: Town stabilization/free cash funds, contrasted with the requested state aid
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman stated the town holds over $9 million in its stabilization account and is also receiving more free cash, but said she is not asking for any of that one-time money, distinguishing it from the recurring state aid she is requesting.

budget_items.topic: Final FY27 warrant article amount for the September 3 special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee voted to amend its warrant article language to request this full amount of additional education receipts for the FY27 operating budget, rather than the previously voted $350,000.

budget_items.topic: Potential additional per-pupil state funding (millionaire's tax)
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman described a further proposal from the governor for $100 million in millionaire's-tax funds for per-pupil aid, which could mean roughly $170,000-$175,000 more for the district if the legislature passes it; the superintendent cautioned it would not be enough to restore multiple lost positions.

budget_items.topic: Custodians' union (AFSCME Council 93) contract economics
budget_items.what_was_said: The new MOU gives custodians a 3.5% increase in FY27 and 2.5% increases in FY28 and FY29, adds longevity steps, converts longevity pay to flat dollar amounts ($500/$1,000/$1,250/$1,750 by years of service), and raises the clothing allowance to $455.

budget_items.topic: Athletic director / assistant principal staffing structure and cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The previously combined half-time athletic director/vice principal role (held by Miss Burns) has been split; the district plans two full-time assistant principals contingent on town meeting appropriating the funds, alongside a new half-time athletic director.

decisions.decision: The district, rather than the football boosters, will pay for extra football helmets, so that donation offer was withdrawn.

Rather than track two competing routes (the citizen petition and a separate school committee article), the committee agreed to take the language of the existing warrant article, amend it, and vote on it as the committee's own article, with Gilman stating she will not separately pursue funding through the citizen petition track.

The Athletic Advisory Committee will be restarted to help coordinate booster-club fundraising and ensure compliance with state/federal requirements; Tony and Mandy will serve on it along with volunteers Peter Beard and others.
The committee will put together an MSBA/Turkey Hill primer presentation for itself and the public ahead of beginning the formal MSBA process.

No regular meeting is planned for August, though a Zoom meeting may be called if needed for line item transfers; the committee will otherwise meet next at a finance committee meeting and then the day before the September 3 special town meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee reviewed FY26 year-end line item transfers, approved several donations (LEAF grants, Musicators, football boosters), heard a detailed presentation on additional FY27 state aid via the cherry sheet, and voted to amend its warrant article for the September 3 "extra special" town meeting from $350,000 to $418,056 in additional state education aid. It also voted to sign a letter to the legislature supporting a further $100 million per-pupil funding proposal, ratified a new custodians' union contract, heard the superintendent's report on hiring and grants, approved a 300th-anniversary fireworks proposal, and discussed the long MSBA process facing Turkey Hill Elementary.
